hero.title: Ship a local actor mesh with a website attached.
hero.body: This mode treats the website as the presentation shell for a Node-hosted actor runtime. Routes, actors, and runtime state all come from manifests that Kain can inspect and write.

feature_cards.title: Node-hosted runtime
feature_cards.body: Local HTTP serving is built into the helper with no external dependency surface.

feature_cards.title: Actor topology as data
feature_cards.body: Route and actor definitions live in manifests and can be reported from Kain.

feature_cards.title: Kain stays in the loop
feature_cards.body: The website runtime is still driven through Kain entrypoints and stdlib wrappers.

story_cards.title: Presentation and runtime together
story_cards.body: The page, APIs, and actor notes all belong to one template lane.

story_cards.title: Ready for websocket or queue adapters
story_cards.body: Add more runtime transports later without changing the manifest model.

timeline.title: Name the actors
timeline.body: Treat responsibilities and channels as first-class design inputs.

timeline.title: Map the HTTP surface
timeline.body: Expose runtime, actor, and chat metadata through stable route manifests.

timeline.title: Use the page as a control room
timeline.body: The website becomes an operational shell instead of a static brochure.

chat_seed.text: I can describe the active routes, actor responsibilities, or next runtime extension points.
